## Sedatives

| Drug                  | Dose                                      | Adverse Reactions                          | Pearls |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|--------|
| **Propofol**<br>GABAa receptor agonist | Max 50 mcg/kg/min                         | Hypotension, Apnea, Movement, Pain at injection site, Hypertriglyceridemia, Pancreatitis, PRIS (hyperkalemia, dysrhythmia, lipemia, metabolic acidosis, heart failure, rhabdomyolysis) | Contraindications: Allergy to soy or egg. Use with caution in cardiovascular disease. Rapid onset/offset. Lipid vehicle susceptible to bacterial contamination — change IV tubing/bottle q12h. Blue-green urine discoloration. Delivers 1.1 kcal/ml. |
| **Dexmedetomidine**<br>Alpha-2 agonist | Maintenance: 0.2-1.4 mcg/kg/h<br>Loading dose (1 mcg/kg) **NOT** recommended | Hypotension, Transient hypotension, severe bradycardia, sinus arrest during loading dose, Bradycardia | Has analgesic properties. Goal is patient arousable with stimulation and sedative state when stimulation removed. Does not require mechanical ventilation. |
| **Lorazepam**<br>GABAa receptor agonist | Loading: 0.02-0.04 mg/kg<br>Intermittent: 0.02-0.06 mg/kg q2-6 h (max 2 mg IV for agitation at 2 mg/min)<br>Maintenance infusion: 0.01-0.1 mg/kg/h | Hypotension, Respiratory depression, Drowsiness, Pain at injection site, Akathisia, Confusion, Anterograde amnesia, Visual disturbances, Paradoxical reactions | Precipitation and metabolic acidosis possible; inline filter recommended for infusions. |
| **Midazolam**<br>GABAa receptor agonist | Loading: 0.01-0.05 mg/kg<br>Maintenance: 0.01-0.1 mg/kg/h | Similar to lorazepam | Rapid onset and short duration. Active metabolites may accumulate in renal dysfunction. |

## Opioids

| Drug         | Usual dose                                      | Adverse Reactions                     | Pearls |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|--------|
| **Fentanyl** | Bolus: 50-100 mcg or 1-2 mcg/kg IV<br>Maintenance: 0.7-10 mcg/kg/hr or 25-700 mcg/h | Respiratory depression, Bradycardia, Edema, Confusion, Sedation, Mood changes, Constipation, Miosis, Chest wall rigidity, Diaphoresis, Myoclonus | May be alternative in morphine allergy. Do not use transdermal in acute setting (delayed onset 6-24 h). |
| **Hydromorphone** | Oral: 2-4 mg q4-6h<br>IV: 0.2-1 mg q4-6h     | Respiratory depression, Bradycardia, Edema, Confusion, Sedation, Mood changes, Constipation, Miosis, Diaphoresis, Myoclonus | May be alternative in morphine allergy. |
| **Morphine** | Bolus: 2-10 mg IVP<br>Intermediate: 2-8 mg q3-4h<br>Maintenance infusion: 0.8-30 | Itching, Respiratory depression, Sedation, Pruritus, Urinary retention, Pain at injection site, Dizziness | Active metabolites accumulate in renal dysfunction — reduced dose recommended. Can induce histamine release causing itching. |

**Naloxone (antagonist)**  
- IV/IM: 0.04-0.4 mg  
- Intranasal: 1-2 mg per naris (repeat q2-3 min, switch to IV/IM)  
**Adverse:** Tachycardia, Hypertension, Nausea, Vomiting, Tremor, Diaphoresis, Dyspnea, Withdrawal symptoms.  
**Pearl:** Short half-life — effects may wear off before opioid cleared (renarcotization risk).

## Neuromuscular Blocking Agents

| Agent              | Dosing                                      | Onset              | Duration                  | Pearls                                      | Adverse Effects |
|--------------------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| **Succinylcholine** | Adults: 0.5-1.1 mg/kg IV<br>IM: 2-4 mg/kg | Very Rapid (IV 30-60s) | Short (3-5 min, max 10 min) | Cannot be reversed. Contraindicated in malignant hyperthermia, hyperkalemia risk. | Hypersensitivity, Anaphylaxis, Cardiac arrest, Hyperkalemia, Rhabdomyolysis |
| **Vecuronium**     | 0.1 mg/kg IV (up to 0.2 mg/kg)             | Prolonged (3-9 min) | Intermediate (35-45 min) | No significant CV effects. No effect on ICP. | Malignant hyperthermia, Hypertension, Hyperkalemia |
| **Cisatracurium**  | 0.15-0.2 mg/kg IV                          | Fast (1.5-2 min)   | Prolonged (45-75 min adults) | Hofmann elimination — good in renal/hepatic failure. | Prolonged respiratory depression, Jaw rigidity |
| **Rocuronium**     | 0.6-1.2 mg/kg IV                           | Rapid (1-2 min)    | Intermediate (20-35 min) | Prolonged in renal failure. | Rhabdomyolysis, Myalgias, Skeletal muscle weakness |

## Vasopressors / Inotropes

| Vasopressor/Inotrope | Adrenergic receptor activation | Initial dosing                  | Indications                          | Advantages                              | Disadvantages |
|----------------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|---------------|
| **Norepinephrine**   | α1, β1                         | 2-5 mcg/min OR 0.02-0.06 mcg/kg/min | Septic shock with low SVR            | Great for increasing SVR/MAP while preserving CO. First line for septic, cardiogenic, hypovolemic shock. | May increase O2 consumption, Myocardial ischemia, Decrease intestinal perfusion |
| **Dopamine**         | D1 (0-5), β1 (5-10), α1 (10-15) | 0-15 mcg/kg/min                | Poor cardiac function, Hypotension with bradycardia | Effective at multiple receptors         | Highest risk of dysrhythmias at high doses |
| **Epinephrine**      | β1, α1, β2                     | 0.02-0.05 mcg/kg/min           | Septic shock with low SVR/CO, Anaphylactic shock | First line for septic shock             | Risk of dysrhythmias, Myocardial ischemia |
| **Phenylephrine**    | α1                             | 10-200 mcg/min OR 0.1-1 mcg/kg/min | Rapid MAP increases post-sedation   | No β effects, less arrhythmogenic       | May decrease CO, Reflex bradycardia |
| **Vasopressin**      | 0                              | 0.02-0.04 units/min            | Refractory hypotension in septic shock | Spares pulmonary vasoconstriction       | May decrease CO in CAD |
| **Dobutamine**       | β1, α1, β2                     | 2.5-10 mcg/kg/min              | Acute decompensated HF               | Improves CO in decompensated HF         | Can decrease SVR, Provoke hypotension |

## Fluids

### Physiologic Properties of Resuscitation Fluids

| Fluid                  | Na mEq/L | K mEq/L | Ca mg/dL | Mg mg/dL | Cl mEq/L | Acetate mEq/L | Lactate mEq/L | Gluconate mEq/L | Bicarb mEq/L | Osmolarity mOsm/L |
|------------------------|----------|---------|----------|----------|----------|---------------|---------------|-----------------|--------------|-------------------|
| **Plasma**             | 135-145  | 3.5-5   | 2.2-2.6  | 0.8-1.0  | 94-111   | -             | 1.2           | -               | -            | 275-295           |
| **Na Cl**              | 154      | -       | -        | -        | 154      | -             | -             | -               | -            | 308               |
| **LR**                 | 130      | 4       | 2.7      | -        | 109      | -             | 28            | -               | -            | 273               |
| **Plasma-Lyte**        | 140      | 5       | -        | 3.0      | 98       | 27            | -             | 23              | -            | 294               |
| **0.45% Na Cl + Na Bicarb** | 141 | -       | -        | -        | 72       | -             | -             | -               | 70           | 283               |

**Key Notes:**  
- Prefer balanced crystalloids (LR, Plasma-Lyte) over normal saline in most neuro ICU patients to avoid hyperchloremic acidosis.  
- Avoid hypotonic fluids in patients at risk for cerebral edema.
